name: nutrient
description: Extract data from PDFs, Office files, images and scans, with page citations and warnings for values to check. Also convert documents to Markdown and classify them. Uses your Nutrient account.

interface.longDescription:
Nutrient extracts data from your documents. It shows where on the page it found the values, and it warns you about values to check. It works with PDFs, Office documents, images and scanned pages, such as invoices, receipts, bank statements, contracts and forms.

What you can do:
- Extract data. Ask for the values you need in plain words, for example an invoice number, a date, a total or the line items. When Nutrient finds a value on the page, it adds a citation to that place. Values without a citation, or with low confidence, get a warning, so you know what to check.
- Check the values. In the ChatGPT and Codex apps, select Review in the Nutrient panel to see the values highlighted on their pages.
- Get the same fields from many files. Nutrient makes an extraction schema (a list of fields) from one sample file. Use it for similar files, and each file returns the same fields.
- Convert documents to Markdown. Headings, tables and reading order stay in place. Scanned pages are read with OCR.
- Classify documents into two or more categories that you name, with a confidence score for each.
- See how many credits are left in your Nutrient account.

In Codex, Nutrient can also work with files on your computer: make searchable PDFs, convert files (for example, Word to PDF), merge them, redact information such as personal data, and add your organization's digital signature to PDFs. Codex saves the new files for you.

Who it's for: people who take data from documents and need to check it, for example in finance, operations or legal work, and developers who want to try the Nutrient API on their own documents. Each run is saved in your Nutrient account, so you can open it again later.

Good to know:
- You need a Nutrient account. Each run uses credits from your account.
- In ChatGPT, Nutrient takes files that you attach to the chat, or HTTPS links. Searchable PDFs, file conversion, merging, redaction and signing are available only in Codex.
- For a summary of a document or a question about it, ChatGPT and Codex read the document themselves. When you ask to extract, convert or classify, they send the file to Nutrient and tell you. To keep a file out of Nutrient, ask them to read it themselves.
- Your documents go only to your Nutrient account. Uploaded files are kept for 24 hours, and runs for your plan's retention period. If you open Review, a copy of the document stays in your Nutrient account until you delete it.
defaultPrompt: With Nutrient, extract the key details from this document into a table and flag any value I should check
With Nutrient, convert this PDF to Markdown and keep its headings and tables
With Nutrient, ask me which fields I need, then extract them from each of these files into one table

positive.description: Extract invoice fields from a PDF link
positive.prompt: Extract the invoice number, invoice date and total from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PSPDFKit/pspdfkit-maui-catalog/main/Resources/Raw/Assets/invoice.pdf
positive.expected_behavior: Nutrient extracts the invoice number 19431-781, the date March 12, 2024 and the total 2,720 € from page 1. Values that Nutrient finds on the page have a citation, and a value without one shows Nutrient's review warning. The Nutrient panel lists the values, and Review shows the cited values highlighted on the page.

positive.description: Convert an attached PDF to Markdown
positive.prompt: Convert the attached menu to Markdown with Nutrient.
positive.expected_behavior: Nutrient parses the attached five-page PDF, and the answer gives the menu as Markdown with its sections, dishes and prices. The Nutrient panel shows the result.

positive.prompt: With Nutrient, is https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PSPDFKit/pspdfkit-maui-catalog/main/Resources/Raw/Assets/default.pdf a contract, an invoice or a form?
positive.expected_behavior: Nutrient labels the document a contract with a confidence score, and the answer names that label.

positive.description: Generate an extraction schema from a sample invoice without extracting
positive.prompt: Use Nutrient to generate an extraction schema for invoices like https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PSPDFKit/pspdfkit-maui-catalog/main/Resources/Raw/Assets/invoice.pdf with the invoice number, date, seller, and line items with quantity and unit price. Don't extract the values yet.
positive.expected_behavior: Nutrient generates a JSON schema from the sample invoice with the requested fields and an array of line items. No values are extracted and no run is stored.

positive.prompt: How many Nutrient Data Extraction credits do I have left?
positive.expected_behavior: Nutrient reports the Data Extraction credits used and remaining in the signed-in account's current billing period.

negative.description: A general question with no document, which Nutrient isn't needed for
negative.prompt: Suggest three names for a coffee shop.

negative.description: Deleting account data, which Nutrient's tools can't do
negative.prompt: Delete every document stored in my Nutrient account.

negative.description: Writing a new document from scratch, which isn't document processing
negative.prompt: Write a short apartment rental agreement I can send to a new tenant.

review.commerce_description: Nutrient sells nothing in ChatGPT. Runs use the credits of the user's existing Nutrient DWS account.

publication.release_notes: First release: extract data from documents with page citations and warnings for values to check, review the values in the Nutrient panel, convert documents to Markdown and classify them, with your Nutrient account.
